task: Fix the memory leak in the HTTP connection pool after the keep-alive setting was changed.

candidate_memories.content: Heap profiler shows HTTP client connections accumulating at 12 per minute; pool is not releasing idle connections.
HTTP client idle connection timeout must be set to 90 seconds; the keep-alive change set it to zero, disabling timeouts.
The keep-alive change was made in sprint 18 to improve throughput but the idle timeout was accidentally cleared.
When changing keep-alive settings, always verify that idle connection timeout is preserved in the same commit.
The memory leak affects all HTTP clients that target external APIs; internal service clients use a separate pool.
The HTTP client library was upgraded from net/http to fasthttp in Q3.
Session 2 note: the API documentation was updated for the new authentication flow.
Old practice: HTTP connection pools were not reused between requests before the pool manager was added.
The CDN configuration uses a 60-second keep-alive for edge connections.
Memory profiling in session 16 showed no leaks in the internal connection pool.
Old HTTP guide: connection pool max size was 100 before the throughput scaling work.
HTTP connection pools must have explicit idle timeouts to prevent file descriptor exhaustion.
The frontend team reported 502 errors during peak traffic in session 20.
Internal service calls use gRPC with connection multiplexing; no HTTP pool is involved.
Session 11 note: external API rate limit was increased from 100 to 500 req/min.
The load balancer uses a 120-second idle connection timeout for upstream connections.
When upgrading HTTP clients, verify all timeout settings are preserved by the new client.
Session 8 note: API retry logic was updated with exponential backoff.
Old performance note: disabling keep-alive improved throughput for short-lived connections.
External API contracts require TLS 1.2 minimum for all connections.
